## Description The main goal of `llama.cpp` is to enable LLM (and MLLM) inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of hardware - locally and in the cloud. The `llama.cpp` project is built on top of the [ggml](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml) library. ## Quick start A few options to get `llama.cpp` installed on your machine: ```bash # curl curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh # powershell irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex ``` - Visit https://llama.app and follow the instructions - Run with Docker - see our [Docker documentation](docs/docker.md) - Download pre-built binaries from the [releases page](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases) - Build from source by cloning this repository - check out [our build guide](docs/build.md) Once installed: ```sh # Download and run a model directly from Hugging Face llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF # Launch OpenAI-compatible API server llama serve -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF ```
VLM session with llama cli Llama Chat, the built-in chat app, against llama serve
## Documentation #### Tools - [cli](tools/cli/README.md) - [completion](tools/completion/README.md) - [server](tools/server/README.md) - [Text-to-speech (TTS) models](docs/multimodal/tts.md) - [GBNF grammars](grammars/README.md) #### Development - [How to build](docs/build.md) - [Running on Docker](docs/docker.md) - [Build on Android](docs/android.md) - [Multi-GPU usage](docs/multi-gpu.md) - [Performance troubleshooting](docs/development/token_generation_performance_tips.md) - [GGML tips & tricks](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/wiki/GGML-Tips-&-Tricks) - [XCFramework](docs/xcframework.md) - [Completions](docs/completions.md) - [Models](docs/models.md) - [Release process](docs/release.md) ## Contributing - Contributors can open PRs - Collaborators will be invited based on contributions - Maintainers can push to branches in the `llama.cpp` repo and merge PRs into the `master` branch - Any help with managing issues, PRs and projects is very appreciated! - Read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information ## Acknowledgements - [yhirose/cpp-httplib](https://github.com/yhirose/cpp-httplib) - Single-header HTTP server, used by `llama-server` - MIT license - [nothings/stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) - Single-header image format decoder, used by multimodal subsystem - Public domain - [nlohmann/json](https://github.com/nlohmann/json) - Single-header JSON library, used by various tools/examples - MIT License - [mackron/miniaudio](https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio) - Single-header audio format decoder, used by multimodal subsystem - Public domain - [sheredom/subprocess.h](https://github.com/sheredom/subprocess.h) - Single-header process launching solution for C and C++ - Public domain

moe-cache : support experts selected on another backend (#33133)

When the experts are selected on another backend than the cache, e.g. the loop passes of inkling2_loop with a layer split, the lookup reads a copy of the ids made by the scheduler, which has no source to read the shape from. Take the experts per token from build_lookup instead.

Fixes #33101

releases.name: b12812
releases.body:
<details open>

metal : check all fused nodes for concurrency (#33175)

* metal : check all fused nodes for concurrency

The concurrency check for a fused group only examined the last node, so
intermediate outputs (e.g. the TOPK_MOE ids/weights) and the group's
sources (e.g. the router logits) were ignored. This allowed the fused
top-k kernel to run concurrently with the router matmul that writes its
input, producing nondeterministic expert routing.

Check every node of the fused group instead.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

* tests : update the Metal fusion baseline for bailingmoe3

PR #33081 enables the SSM_CONV + SILU fusion in bailingmoe3. Record the
new SSM_CONV+UNARY count in the Metal baseline.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

<details open>

ui: share conversations to Hugging Face datasets as agent traces (#32608)

* ui: add @ggml-org/llama-huggingface, a Hugging Face account as a package

A package in ui/lib that gives an app running in the browser, with no
server of its own, a Hugging Face account. Its plain entry holds "Sign in
with Hugging Face" (OAuth with PKCE and dynamic client registration) and
the Hub calls: who the account is, its datasets, and committing a trace
file to one. Its Svelte entry holds the account as state (HfAccount) and
the components that show it, built on Llama UI: the account panel and the
dialog that shares a trace.

It knows no app: the app says who it is and hands over what to share.
Llama Chat compiles it from source, like the other packages, so the
llama-server image builds (.devops) and the asset staging
(scripts/ui-assets.cmake) copy its sources next to the other packages'.
CI checks and tests it.

Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium)

llama.cpp

LLM inference in C/C++

v1.0.0 / ggml / ops / maintainer PRs / dev stats / lib llama API / llama-server REST API

Description

The main goal of llama.cpp is to enable LLM (and MLLM) inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of hardware - locally and in the cloud.

The llama.cpp project is built on top of the ggml library.

Quick start

A few options to get llama.cpp installed on your machine:

# curl
curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh

# powershell
irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex
  • Visit https://llama.app and follow the instructions
  • Run with Docker - see our Docker documentation
  • Download pre-built binaries from the releases page
  • Build from source by cloning this repository - check out our build guide

Once installed:

# Download and run a model directly from Hugging Face
llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF

# Launch OpenAI-compatible API server
llama serve -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF
VLM session with llama cli Llama Chat, the built-in chat app, against llama serve

aiSummary.oneLiner: A highly optimized C/C++ inference engine for running large language models locally on consumer hardware.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project provides a standalone implementation for evaluating large language models directly on standard consumer hardware. It achieves remarkable performance by eschewing heavy Python dependencies in favor of pure C and C++ execution. The engine supports diverse hardware backends, dynamically allocating tensor operations across available CPUs and GPUs to maximize throughput. It implements advanced quantization techniques, drastically reducing memory requirements without significantly compromising model accuracy. Developers can integrate the engine into diverse applications using its extensive bindings and the bundled HTTP server.
keyFeatures: Hardware acceleration: Supports execution across Apple Silicon, NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, and standard x86 CPUs.
Model quantization: Implements integer quantization formats from 1.5-bit to 8-bit to reduce VRAM consumption dramatically.
Zero dependencies: Compiles as a single standalone executable without requiring external Python environments or heavy frameworks.
Continuous batching: Processes multiple concurrent inference requests efficiently through the bundled OpenAI-compatible server.
Extensive bindings: Provides wrappers for numerous programming languages including Python, Go, Rust, and Node.js.

useCases.title: Local development
useCases.description: Run advanced language models locally on a standard laptop to prototype AI applications without incurring API costs.

useCases.title: Edge deployment
useCases.description: Deploy highly optimized conversational agents directly onto resource-constrained edge devices and mobile phones.

useCases.title: Serverless endpoints
useCases.description: Host private OpenAI-compatible API endpoints locally using the provided HTTP server binary.

useCases.title: Application integration
useCases.description: Embed advanced language processing capabilities directly into desktop software using native language bindings.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI developers and researchers seeking to execute large language models efficiently without relying on cloud providers. Software engineers embedding local intelligence into consumer applications across diverse hardware platforms.
